start.title: Make sure alarms can reach you

topics.title: Start or connect your sensor
topics.for: Readings from your Libre 2 or 2 Plus straight into Sukoon, no other app needed.
topics.summary: Readings straight into Sukoon, no other app.

steps.text: Put the sensor on as usual.
Start it from the Sensor page.
steps.path: You › Sensor › Start a new sensor

steps.text: Hold the top of your phone flat on the sensor until it says Started.
Wait an hour: Now counts down to the first reading.
Pair it again.
Hold the phone on it until it buzzes. The last 8 hours appear at once.

tips: A sensor talks to one phone at a time. Pairing Sukoon takes it from LibreLink or DiaBox; scanning it in that app takes it back.
Check sensor only reads it: its state, its day and its value now.
“Lost it for a moment”? Keep the phone still; it carries on by itself.

fixes.fix: Use Start a new sensor, not Pair again.
It's time for a new sensor.

topics.title: Now: your number at a glance
topics.for: Knowing where you are and what to do, in one look.
topics.summary: Where you are and what to do, in one look.

steps.text: The big number is your newest reading; the arrow is where it's heading.
The colour says low, in your range or high. The message under it says what matters now, and one next step.
The buttons at the top log food and insulin; “u active” is rapid insulin still working.
Today (the sliders button) pauses alarms or starts a workout, a fast or a sick day. The chips under the header show what's on.

tips: A reading older than 10 minutes turns grey and is never shown as current.
In a sensor's first hour, any reading shows in grey and counts for nothing: no alarms, reports or AI.
Pull down to bring in the latest MyFitnessPal meals.

topics.title: Keep Sukoon running
topics.for: Alarms that reach you at 3 a.m. too.
topics.summary: Alarms that reach you at 3 a.m. too.

steps.text: Allow everything Setup lists.
On Samsung or Xiaomi, also open the phone's Settings › Apps › Sukoon and set Battery to Unrestricted; on Xiaomi turn on Autostart too.
Leave Sukoon's small notification on: it keeps Sukoon running and shows your number.

tips: If the phone stops Sukoon anyway, a watchdog wakes it and the no-readings alarm sounds.
After a restart or an update it reconnects by itself within a minute or two.
Keep the phone within a few metres; a body or a wall shortens that. The Connection note on the Sensor page counts the last day's gaps.

topics.title: Safety first
topics.for: What Sukoon is, and isn't.
topics.summary: What Sukoon is, and isn't.

steps.text: Sukoon is not a medical device. If a number doesn't match how you feel, check with a finger-prick.
Follow your care team on treatment. Dose suggestions are a beta: maths on your own numbers, nothing more.
In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

topics.title: Alarms
topics.for: Hearing about a low or a high before it becomes a problem.
topics.summary: Hear about a low or a high early.

steps.text: Set your low and high lines, and turn each alarm on or off.
Pick a sound pack (Astral, Orbit, Glass, Clear or Bells), or a phone sound or your own file for any alarm.
Try each one with See and hear each alarm.
Check Can alarms reach you? It lists anything blocking them, with a fix for each.

tips: Urgent low (under 55) is always on and can't be moved: it fills the screen and repeats every 5 minutes until you answer.
While a low sounds, the alarm volume is lifted, and put back after.
I'm treating it starts the 15-minute wait, then checks on you again.
Highs can stay quiet at night; lows never do.

fixes.fix: Open Can alarms reach you? and What your alarms did, both in You › Alarms & sounds.

topics.title: Emergency contacts
topics.for: Someone being told when you can't answer.
topics.summary: Someone is told when you can't answer.

steps.text: Add a contact from your phone book, or type a number.
Allow SMS and calls when the setup check asks.
Choose how long an urgent low may go unanswered (10 minutes by default).
An urgent low, or lost signal while low, goes unanswered for that long.
A 60-second countdown fills the screen, with a loud sound and I'm OK.
Everyone gets a text and the first contact gets a call; again after 30 minutes if there's still no answer.
Back to 70 or more, they get a “back to normal” text.

tips: Any answer, even swiping the alarm away, restarts the clock.
On Now, Alert my emergency contact texts, WhatsApps or calls them yourself.

topics.title: Snooze or pause?
topics.for: Quieting one alarm, or all of them for a while.
topics.summary: Quiet one alarm, or all of them for a while.

steps.text: Snooze quiets the alarm that's sounding, for the minutes set for it. The other alarms keep watching.
Pause quiets every alarm but urgent low, for 30 minutes to 4 hours: a workout, a meeting.
While they're paused, a chip on Now says until when. Tap it to turn them back on.

tips: Urgent low is never paused: it repeats every 5 minutes until you answer.
Under the parent lock, pausing asks for the PIN.

topics.title: Log a meal
topics.for: Knowing what went in, so the numbers make sense later.
topics.summary: What went in, so the numbers make sense.

steps.text: Start a meal from the food button on Now.
Find what you ate: search (yours first, then home dishes, then Open Food Facts), the barcode button, a photo, or just carbs.
Set How much? for each food; the plate adds it up.
Add the insulin you took for it on the same screen, and save.

tips: Ask the AI estimates any dish from its name or photos, with your own Gemini key.
A barcode that isn't found can be added as your own; the next scan finds it.
Every entry shows your glucose at that moment; meals show what they did to it afterwards.
Saved by mistake? Undo on the confirmation.

topics.title: Insulin and dose suggestions
topics.for: Logging doses quickly, and a suggested dose with its maths if you want one.
topics.summary: Quick doses, and the maths if you want it.

steps.text: Log a dose: rapid or long-acting, the amount, and Where? if you like.
“u active” on Now is rapid insulin still working (5 hours by default).
For dose suggestions (beta), turn them on and fill your ratio per meal, correction factor, target and maximum.

tips: A suggestion shows its maths; Use puts it in the amount, and only Save logs it.
No suggestion under 70, or under 100 and falling: treat that first (15 g).
Learning from your meals shows what your meals say about your ratios. Nothing changes until you press Use, and then by at most 20%.
Under 18, suggestions only turn on behind a parent lock.

topics.title: Learning from your meals
topics.for: Seeing what your own meals say about your ratios.
topics.summary: What your meals say about your ratios.

steps.text: Open Learning.
Each meal gets a verdict; clean ones teach a ratio per meal time.
When a number is ready, Use moves yours toward it, by at most 20% at a time.

tips: A meal counts when it has insulin with it, readings before and 4 hours after, and nothing else eaten or injected around it.
How to make a meal count lists exactly what's needed.

topics.title: Long-acting reminder
topics.for: Never wondering “did I take it?”.
topics.summary: Never wonder “did I take it?”.

steps.text: Turn the reminder on and pick your time.
If no long-acting was logged in the 12 hours before, a notification comes at that time.
Took it logs your usual amount; In 30 min waits.

tips: It comes back every 30 minutes, 3 times, and goes as soon as the dose is logged anywhere.
The Insulin widget has Took it too.

topics.title: Say it
topics.for: Logging a meal, insulin or a workout by speaking, in your own words.
topics.summary: Log by speaking, in your own words.

steps.text: Add your free Gemini key once: Say it uses the AI assistant.
Tap + in the Logbook, then Say it.
Say what you ate, took or did, like “koshari, a big plate, 6 units”. Check what it heard, correct anything, and Save.

tips: Nothing is saved until you press Save.
Carbs for a low are marked as a treatment.

topics.title: Supplies
topics.for: Knowing when your pens run out, and when to pick up more.
topics.summary: When your pens run out, and the next pickup.

steps.text: Enter how many pens of each kind you have.
Sukoon counts them down from the doses you log, as days left.
Set your next pickup and when to be reminded.

tips: When a kind runs low, a chip on Now says so.

topics.title: Injection sites
topics.for: Moving your injections around, so insulin works the same every time.
topics.summary: Move injections around so insulin works evenly.

steps.text: When you log insulin, tap Where? and the spot on the body map (your left is on the left).
The dashed ring is the spot that has rested longest: a good next choice.
See the last 30 days as a map.

tips: The same spot again and again can form lumps under the skin that take up insulin unevenly.
Belly is fastest (a few centimetres from the navel), then the back of the upper arms, outer thighs and upper outer buttocks.

topics.title: MyFitnessPal and Health Connect
topics.for: Meals you log in MyFitnessPal showing up in Sukoon, with every nutrient.
topics.summary: MyFitnessPal meals in Sukoon, every nutrient.

steps.text: In MyFitnessPal: More › Apps & Devices › Health Connect › Connect, and allow everything.
In Sukoon, allow Health Connect.
Pull down on Now or the Logbook to bring the latest in.

tips: Workouts of 10 minutes or more, steps and water come in the same way; your readings go out to Health Connect.
MyFitnessPal shares one running total a day, so Sukoon splits it into meals by when you logged them.

fixes.fix: You › Apps & data › Resync says how many MyFitnessPal meals Health Connect has. None? Update MyFitnessPal and connect again.

topics.title: Workouts, fasting, sick days and your goal
topics.for: What Sukoon changes while you train, fast or are ill, and why.
topics.summary: Today, your goal, and the numbers behind them.

steps.text: Start a workout from Today: the low alarm sits at 100 while it lasts (Moser et al. 2020).
Lifting can raise glucose now and lower it for at least a day after (Riddell et al. 2017). After any workout, logged or started from Today, the low alarm sits at 80 overnight.
Before starting: under 90, have 10–20 g and wait; 90–125, about 10 g; over 270, check ketones first (Riddell 2017).
Dose suggestions: the meal after a workout 50% lower by default; corrections during and just after halved (lifting rises, Moser 2020). Nothing is cut before lifting.
Lean bulk: +100–300 kcal a day, protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg, gaining 0.25–0.5% of your weight a week (Iraki et al. 2019).

Cut: at most 500 kcal under maintenance, losing 0.5–1% a week, protein 2.2–2.6 g/kg (Helms et al. 2014; Murphy & Koehler 2022). Eating less usually means less insulin: review your doses with your clinic.
Maintain: protein 1.4–2.0 g/kg (ISSN 2017).
Maintenance is estimated from your weight, height, age and sex (Mifflin–St Jeor × 1.55). If you know yours, type it in.
Set your Fajr and Maghrib times once, then switch Fasting on in Today on the days you fast.
Break the fast under 70 or over 300, or if you feel unwell; at 70–90, check again within the hour (IDF-DAR 2021).
Suhoor meal dose suggested 30% lower; none during the fast. Long-acting: IDF-DAR says take it at iftar, 30–40% less (15–30% for Toujeo in its table). Agree any change with your doctor.
Switch Sick day on in Today: a ketone reminder every 2 hours, and high alarms every hour.
Never stop long-acting insulin; drink about 100 ml an hour (ISPAD 2022).
Ketones (mmol/L): under 0.6 normal; 0.6–1.4 check again in 1–2 h; 1.5–2.9 extra rapid insulin as your plan says; 3.0 or more, vomiting or fast breathing: urgent care.

tips: Fat-heavy meals (tahina, eggs, oil) rise 3–5 hours later. A split dose may suit them: agree it with your doctor.
Creatine can make lows a little more likely and raises creatinine: ask for a cystatin-C kidney test.
Sleep 7–8 hours: one short night cuts muscle building by about 18%.

topics.title: Graph, Insights and Report
topics.for: Seeing the patterns behind the days.
topics.summary: The patterns behind the days.

steps.text: Any range from 3 hours to 14 days, any past day, with time in range and GMI (an A1C estimate).
One thing worth doing, with the button that does it, and a few things worth knowing.
The one-page summary clinics use, as a PDF to share.

tips: Insights are observations, never instructions.
A sensor's first hour is left out of all three.

topics.title: Ask Sukoon
topics.for: Questions about your own readings and logs, answered in plain words.
topics.summary: Your readings and logs, in plain words.

steps.text: Add your free Gemini key once.
Ask anything, or tap a suggestion.

tips: Answers use your last 7 days of real readings and your logbook; the line under the title says exactly what.
The key stays on this phone. Not medical advice.

topics.title: Your range
topics.for: A range that matches your goals.
topics.summary: A range that matches your goals.

steps.text: Choose the top of your range, 120 to 180 (the bottom stays 70).
Now, the graph's colours and time in range follow it; reports also keep the international 70–180.

tips: Moving the top can move your high alarm with it.

topics.title: Calibration
topics.for: Nudging the sensor toward your finger-pricks, when it's clearly off.
topics.summary: Nudge the sensor toward your finger-pricks.

steps.text: Log finger-pricks while your glucose is steady.
Turn calibration on.

tips: Off by default: the sensor's own calibration is usually best.
It uses up to 4 steady finger-pricks from the last 7 days, stays within ±20 mg/dL and ×0.8–1.25, and never raises a low.

topics.title: Clinic visit
topics.for: Getting the most out of your next appointment.
topics.summary: Your next visit, what to ask, your labs.

steps.text: Set the date of your next visit.
Questions to ask come from your insights and from labs that are due; add your own.
Log your lab results, like HbA1c.
Share the report with your doctor: it carries the questions and labs too.

topics.title: Share with family
topics.for: The people who'd want to know, seeing your number live.
topics.summary: Family sees your number live.

steps.text: Make an account (email and password).
Invite someone to follow you: send the link, or let them scan the QR code. It works once, for 24 hours.
On Android the link opens Sukoon with the code filled in: one tap to follow. On an iPhone it opens the follow page, which follows once they sign in.
Choose which of your alarms sound on their phones. Urgent low always does.
steps.path: You › People › Alarms your followers get

tips: Only real readings are shared, never demo data. Either side can end a follow.
On an iPhone, alarms sound only while the follow page is open: keep emergency contacts set too.

topics.title: Follow someone
topics.for: Watching a child's or parent's glucose, with their alarms on your phone.
topics.summary: Their glucose and alarms on your phone.

steps.text: Enter the code from their invite.
Now shows their number, chart and words; Trends shows their graph, insights and report.
Turn on Alert me about them, and their alarms sound here with their name.
steps.path: You › People › Alert me about them

tips: Answering their alarm only snoozes it on your phone. Emergency texts are never sent from a follower's phone.

topics.title: LibreLinkUp and Dexcom
topics.for: Following people on Abbott's or Dexcom's apps, or using one as your own glucose.
topics.summary: Follow people on Abbott's or Dexcom's apps.

steps.text: Sign in to LibreLinkUp or Dexcom.
LibreLinkUp: in their Libre app, Connected apps › LibreLinkUp › add your email. Dexcom: Share on in their Dexcom app.
To make one your own glucose (a Libre 3, say), pick it as the source.

tips: Both come through the internet, about a minute (LibreLinkUp) or five (Dexcom) behind the sensor.

topics.title: Parent lock
topics.for: A child's phone where the important settings can't be changed by accident or on purpose.
topics.summary: A child can't change what matters.

steps.text: Set a 4–8 digit PIN, typed twice.
steps.path: You › your name at the top › Parent lock

steps.text: From then on, changing alarms, the range, doses or the profile asks for it, once per visit.

tips: It also guards everything that would cut a parent off: which alarms followers get, sharing, removing a follower, signing out and deleting the account.
It's for children only: from 18 (the age in About you) it no longer applies.
Removing it needs the PIN.

topics.title: Widgets
topics.for: Your number on the home screen, without opening anything.
topics.summary: Your number on the home screen.

steps.text: Open the widget maker.
Pick a style, a size and a background; the preview is the real widget.
Add to home screen.

tips: Long-press a widget to edit it. An old reading greys out, never shown as current.

topics.title: Backup, moving phones and your data
topics.for: Never losing your history, and knowing where it goes.
topics.summary: Never lose your history.

steps.text: Back up everything to one private file: readings, logbook, settings, sensor pairing and photos.
steps.path: You › Export & backup › Back up everything

steps.text: On a new phone, Restore that file and Sukoon opens as it was (widgets need adding again).
Optional: a daily backup to Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox.

tips: Nothing leaves your phone unless you turn it on: Nightscout, the AI with your own key, followers, Health Connect.
Notices from Sukoon may appear on Now: news about the app, read every 6 hours from Sukoon's site, with nothing about you sent.
The full list is in the privacy policy, in You › Help & about.
